findings.problem: The named spec still assigns merging `wb run remote-runner submit`/`fetch` with `submit-remote-job`/`fetch-remote-output` to this plan. This split version has no such scope, increment, named remote-runner/mempalace specs, or replacement plan reference, so it drifts from its source spec and leaves the assigned work unplanned.
findings.suggestion: Restore a decision/build increment for the pairing and name the affected specs, or first make an owner-approved decision/spec update that explicitly reassigns it to one of the split plans and names that plan.

findings.problem: The plan-wide constraint requires every behavior change to update the affected specs in the same commit, but B changes four commands and C changes six more without listing or stepping any spec updates. E postpones those updates until after the implementation and walk-through. That would knowingly leave current specifications false between increments, contrary to the plan and to the existing terminal-only/`none` descriptions in the named specs.
findings.suggestion: For B and C, name the applicable specification files as affected areas and add same-commit update steps; reserve E for reconciling remaining intended text and recording the completed evidence.

findings.problem: The proposed walk-through treats a throwaway project as sufficient for every command. `wb approve` changes the machine-wide guarded-store approval records, and other commands can change guarded-store state; a throwaway project does not isolate those writes. The plan therefore lacks a safe, reproducible verification arrangement and could leave real owner state changed by a test.
findings.suggestion: Specify an isolated test store/home supported by the test harness (or an explicitly approved disposable store) for the walkthrough, enumerate each non-project write it contains, and record cleanup/retention expectations.

summary: The plan still drifts from the command-permissions assignment for remote checkpoint pairing, postpones required spec updates beyond behavior changes, and lacks isolation for store-mutating walkthroughs.
